package_info.why_malicious: Maven versions prior to 3.8.1 allow the use of custom repositories over HTTP, enabling attackers to perform man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacks, domain hijacking, and download hijacking by redirecting dependency downloads to malicious servers. This undermines the integrity of the Java build process and exposes developers to supply chain attacks.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time (dependency resolution), the code instructs Maven to fetch dependencies from an external HTTP repository, causing Maven to send dependency requests over an unencrypted channel to a potentially attacker-controlled server, resulting in possible interception or replacement of artifacts and compromise of the build process.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Specifying an HTTP (not HTTPS) repository for dependency resolution exposes the build process to interception and tampering, as HTTP traffic can be manipulated by attackers in transit.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Maven repositories should use HTTPS to ensure integrity and authenticity; using HTTP breaks the chain of trust and allows for artifact manipulation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Internal company repositories may use HTTP in isolated, trusted environments, but this is not recommended and should be strictly controlled.
key_indicators: Repository URL uses HTTP instead of HTTPS
Repository is not a well-known or trusted domain
Repository is defined in a transitive dependency POM
Presence of <repository> or <pluginRepository> with <url>http://...</url> in pom.xml

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time (dependency resolution), the code configures Maven to redirect all repository requests to an attacker-controlled HTTP mirror, causing all dependency downloads to be routed through an unencrypted channel to a malicious server, enabling interception or replacement of all dependencies and full compromise of the build process.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Redirecting all repository traffic to an HTTP mirror controlled by an attacker allows for complete compromise of the build process, as all dependencies can be intercepted or replaced.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Mirrors should use HTTPS and point to trusted, official sources; using HTTP and an unknown domain is highly suspicious and violates best practices for supply chain security.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Organizations may use internal mirrors for caching, but these should use HTTPS and be properly secured and restricted to trusted networks.
key_indicators: Mirror URL uses HTTP instead of HTTPS
MirrorOf set to '*' (all repositories), redirecting all traffic
Mirror points to an untrusted or external domain

attack_chain.action: A malicious or compromised POM or settings file specifies an HTTP repository or mirror.
attack_chain.leads_to: Maven attempts to download dependencies from the attacker-controlled HTTP endpoint.

attack_chain.action: Attacker intercepts or replaces dependency artifacts during the build process (MITM or direct control).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is injected into the build, or legitimate dependencies are replaced with trojanized versions.

attack_chain.action: Compromised artifacts are executed as part of the application, leading to code execution, data exfiltration, or further compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: compromise of developer or production systems.

behavioral_signatures: Maven build process connecting to HTTP (not HTTPS) repositories or mirrors
Presence of repository or mirror definitions using HTTP in pom.xml or settings.xml
Unexpected or untrusted domains in repository/mirror URLs
Maven build logs showing dependency downloads from HTTP endpoints
file_indicators: Transitive dependency POMs referencing HTTP repositories
settings.xml or pom.xml referencing domains not associated with Maven Central or trusted internal repositories
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP requests to non-localhost domains during Maven builds
Connections to domains not associated with Maven Central or trusted internal repositories
Unencrypted (HTTP) traffic to external servers during dependency resolution
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan all pom.xml and settings.xml files (including transitive dependencies) for repository or mirror URLs using HTTP. Monitor Maven build logs and network traffic for HTTP requests to external or untrusted domains. Flag builds that attempt to download dependencies over HTTP or from untrusted sources. Enforce policies requiring HTTPS for all external repositories and mirrors. Alert on any repository or mirror configuration that uses HTTP or references unknown domains.
